Rashi on Nazir 3b:10:1.hebrew: אפילו לא נזר אלא מאחד מהן - או מן חרצן או מן זג — הרי זה נזיר, וכל דקדוקי נזירות עליו:
Rashi on Nazir 3b:10:1.english: Even if he took a nazirite vow [to abstain] from only one of them - Either from a grape seed or from a grape skin — he is a nazirite, and all the details of naziriteship are incumbent upon him.

Rashi on Nazir 3b:11:1.hebrew: מכל אשר יעשה - משמע שצריך שיהא נוזר מכל אשר יעשה, שאינו נזיר אלא א"כ נוזר מכולם:
Rashi on Nazir 3b:11:1.english: From anything that is made - This implies that he must vow to abstain from anything that is made [of the grapevine], for he is not a nazirite unless he vows to abstain from all of them.

Rashi on Nazir 3b:11:2.hebrew: אמר קרא מיין ושכר יזיר - דמשמע דאפילו דלא נזר אלא מיין לחודיה, הוי נזיר מכולם:
Rashi on Nazir 3b:11:2.english: The verse states: “He shall abstain from wine and strong drink” - Which implies that even if he only took a nazirite vow from wine alone, he is a nazirite with regard to all of them.

Rashi on Nazir 3b:13:1.english: To prohibit wine of a mitzva like optional wine: What is it — kiddush and havdala? - Does the prohibition of naziriteship take effect upon it?

Rashi on Nazir 3b:1:1.hebrew: ורבנן סברי לא מתפיס איניש במידי דסמיך ליה - ולא אמרי' שבדעתו היה לומר גידול שער, אי לאו דמפרש בהדיא, ואע"ג דנזיר עובר לפניו:
Rashi on Nazir 3b:1:1.english: And the Rabbis hold [that] a person does not associate with something juxtaposed to it - And we do not say that it was his intention to say "growing hair" unless he explicitly specifies [it], even though a nazirite was passing before him.

Rashi on Nazir 3b:2:1.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan says that everyone [agrees] that one does not associate - A person [does not associate] with something that is juxtaposed to it.

Rashi on Nazir 3b:2:2.hebrew: אלא היינו טעמא דר"מ דחיישינן - כי אמר הרי עלי ציפורין, דדלמא קאמר שבדעתו לקבל עליו מידי דזימנין דמייתי עליה צפורים, דהיינו נזירות, דלכי מיטמא מייתי צפרים. בנזיר טמא כתיב: וכי ימות מת עליו בפתע פתאום כו', וביום השמיני יביא שתי תורים, והזיר לה' את ימי נזרו וגו' (במדבר ו׳:י״ב):
Rashi on Nazir 3b:2:2.english: Rather, this is the reason of Rabbi Meir, that we are concerned - When he said, "Behold, birds are upon me" — that perhaps he meant that it was his intention to accept upon himself something for which one sometimes brings birds, namely naziriteship, for when [a nazirite] becomes ritually impure, he brings birds. Regarding an impure nazirite it is written: "And if a person dies beside him suddenly, unexpectedly..." etc., "and on the eighth day he shall bring two turtledoves," "and he shall consecrate to the Lord the days of his naziriteship..." etc. (Numbers 6:12).

Rashi on Nazir 3b:3:1.hebrew: מכדי חיישינן קאמר - כלומר, דלא הוי נזיר אלא משום דאמרי' שמא צפרי נזיר טמא קבל עליו. ואי בתר חששא אזלינן, ליחוש דילמא צפרי נדבה קיבל עליו; ולא ניתנה נזירות אלא להפלאה, ואמאי קאמר ר"מ דהוי נזיר כלל:
Rashi on Nazir 3b:3:1.english: Now, since he says "we are concerned" - That is to say, that he is not [considered] a nazirite except because we say: Perhaps he accepted upon himself the birds of an impure nazirite. And if we follow [mere] apprehension, let us be concerned that perhaps he accepted upon himself voluntary bird-offerings; and naziriteship was given only for explicit articulation [hafla'ah], so why did Rabbi Meir say that he is a nazirite at all?

Rashi on Nazir 3b:3:2.hebrew: א"כ - דבעי למימר צפרי נדבה, הוה אמר: ״הרי עלי קן״, ד״קן״ משמע צפרי נדבה; אבל כי אומר: ״הרי עלי צפורים״, לא משמע צפרי נדבה כלל. הלכך, מדקאמר ״צפורין״, ליכא לספוקי אלא בצפורי נזיר:
Rashi on Nazir 3b:3:2.english: If so - For had he intended to say voluntary bird-offerings, he would have said, "Behold, a nest is upon me," for "nest" implies voluntary bird-offerings; but when he says, "Behold, birds are upon me," it does not imply voluntary bird-offerings at all. Therefore, since he said "birds," there is no [room] for doubt except regarding the birds of a nazirite.

Rashi on Nazir 3b:4:1.hebrew: ודלמא - מקבל עליו תורת ציפורי מצורע: לטבול החיה בדם השחוטה, ולשלחן, ולעשותן כהלכות צפרי מצורע. והך פירכא דפרכינן השתא, קא פריך בין לרבי יוחנן בין לר"ל: דמכדי צפרים סתם קאמר, הא איכא למיחש נמי לצפורי מצורע:
Rashi on Nazir 3b:4:1.english: And perhaps - [That] he accepts upon himself the ritual of the birds of a leper: to dip the live [bird] in the blood of the slaughtered [one], and to send them [away], and to perform them according to the laws of the birds of a leper. And this objection that we raise now is raised both according to Rabbi Yoḥanan and according to Reish Lakish: for since he said "birds" without qualification, behold, there is reason to be concerned about the birds of a leper as well.

Rashi on Nazir 3b:4:2.hebrew: ודלמא נזיר טמא - הוה, וקאמר לאיתויי צפורים ולפוטרו הוא במקומו:
Rashi on Nazir 3b:4:2.english: And perhaps an impure nazirite - [It] was [an impure nazirite who was passing before him], and [the speaker] was saying [this in order] to bring birds and exempt him, [bringing them] himself in his place.

Rashi on Nazir 3b:4:3.hebrew: כגון שהיה נזיר טהור עובר לפניו - דלאו בר אתויי הוא, והלכך, כי אמר ״צפורין״, לא אמר אלא אדעתא דליהוי נזיר כמותו:
Rashi on Nazir 3b:4:3.english: For example, where a pure nazirite was passing before him - For he is not subject to bringing [birds], and therefore, when he said "birds," he said [it] only with the intention of becoming a nazirite like him.

Rashi on Nazir 3b:5:1.hebrew: מאי בינייהו - בין לרבי יוחנן בין לר"ל, לא מיתרצא שמעתתא אלא כגון שנזיר טהור עובר לפניו, משום דאית ליה למיפרך בה כל הני פירוכין, ותריצנא: כגון דנזיר טהור עובר לפניו עסקינן. מה לי אי משום צפרין סמוכין לשיער, אי משום צפרי נזיר טמא — אי משום הכי, אי משום הכי, הוה ליה נזיר:
Rashi on Nazir 3b:5:1.english: What is [the difference] between them - Whether according to Rabbi Yoḥanan or according to Reish Lakish, the sugya could not be resolved except [in a case] where a pure nazirite was passing before him, because all these objections can be raised against it, and we resolved: We are dealing with [a case where] a pure nazirite was passing before him. What difference does it make whether [it is] because of birds juxtaposed to hair, or whether [it is] because of the birds of an impure nazirite — whether for this [reason] or for that [reason], he is a nazirite.

Rashi on Nazir 3b:6:1.hebrew: איכא בינייהו כגון דאמר צפרין סמוכין לשיער - ר' יוחנן סבר: אע"ג דאמר הכי, לא מוכחא מילתא דלקבולי עליה נזירות הוא דקאמר, אלא לקבל עליו צפרין סתם בלא נזירות, אי לאו דנזיר עובר לפניו:
Rashi on Nazir 3b:6:1.english: There is [a difference] between them in [a case] where he said, "Birds juxtaposed to hair" - Rabbi Yoḥanan holds: Even though he said this, it is not evident that he was saying [this] to accept naziriteship upon himself, but rather to accept upon himself birds generally without naziriteship, were it not that a nazirite was passing before him.

Rashi on Nazir 3b:7:1.hebrew: האומר ימין - שלא אוכל ככר זה, הרי זו שבועה:
Rashi on Nazir 3b:7:1.english: One who says: “Right” - [For example,] “[Right,] that I will not eat this loaf [of bread],” this is an oath.

Rashi on Nazir 3b:7:2.english: What is the reason? Is it not because it is written: “And he raised his right hand and his left hand to heaven, and swore by Him Who lives forever”? - For he associates “his right hand” with “and swore,” which is adjacent to it.

Rashi on Nazir 3b:8:1.hebrew: לא - ימין שאוכל ככר זה — כאומר שבועה שאוכל ככר זה דמי, שנאמר: ״נשבע ה' בימינו״ — בימינו אמר, ונחשב כשבועה:
Rashi on Nazir 3b:8:1.english: No - [One who says:] “[By the] right hand that I will eat this loaf” is considered like one who says: “[It is an] oath that I will eat this loaf.” As it is stated: “The Lord has sworn by His right hand” — he said “[by] His right hand,” and it is considered an oath.

Rashi on Nazir 3b:8:2.hebrew: שנאמר ובזרוע עוזו - מדכתיב ימינו וכתיב ובזרוע עוזו, אלמא דזרועו היינו שמאלו. והכי נמי אמרי' בפרק קמא דמסכת ברכות (דף ו.): מנין שהקב"ה מניח תפילין? דכתיב: ובזרוע עוזו, ואין עוזו אלא תפילין כו', ותפילין בשמאל קיימי:
Rashi on Nazir 3b:8:2.english: As it is stated: "And by the arm of His strength" - Since it is written: "His right hand," and it is written: "And by the arm of His strength," evidently "His arm" refers to His left [hand]. And so too we say in the first chapter of Tractate Berakhot (page 6a): From where [is it derived] that the Holy One, Blessed be He, puts on tefillin? As it is written: "And by the arm of His strength," and "His strength" means nothing other than tefillin, etc., and tefillin are placed on the left [arm].

Rashi on Nazir 3b:9:1.hebrew: אמר הריני נזיר מן החרצנים - או שאמר הריני נזיר מן הזגין כו', הרי הוא כמי שאמר הריני נזיר סתם, שמקבל עליו כל דקדוקי נזירות:
Rashi on Nazir 3b:9:1.english: [If] one said: "I am hereby a nazirite from grape seeds" - Or if he said: "I am hereby a nazirite from grape skins," etc., he is like one who said: "I am hereby a nazirite" without qualification, who accepts upon himself all the details of naziriteship.

Tosafot on Nazir 3b:10:1.hebrew: עד שיזיר מכולן - או יאמר סתמא, דמשמע: כל מילי דנזירות קיבל עליה; ואם בא לפרש חרצן וזג — צריך לפרש כולם, גם תגלחת וטומאה:
Tosafot on Nazir 3b:10:1.english: "Until he vows [to abstain] from all of them" - Or he states [his vow] without specification, which implies that he accepted all matters of naziriteship upon himself; but if he comes to specify grape seed and grape skin, he must specify all of them, also shaving and ritual impurity.

Tosafot on Nazir 3b:11:1.hebrew: מכל אשר יעשה מגפן היין - אלמא דמכולהו צריך להזיר. וא"ת: ואכתי תגלחת וטומאה לא שמעינן? וי"ל: כיון דגלי לן ביין, ה"ה שצריך לקבל גם תגלחת וטומאה; ונפקא לן מלישנא דקרא — "מכל":
Tosafot on Nazir 3b:11:1.english: "From all that is made of the grapevine" - Evidently, he must vow to abstain from all of them. And if you say: But still, we have not derived [the requirement for] shaving and ritual impurity? And one can say: Since [the verse] revealed to us regarding wine, the same applies that he must also accept shaving and ritual impurity; and we derive this from the wording of the verse: "From all."

Tosafot on Nazir 3b:11:2.hebrew: מיין ושכר יזיר - משמע: אפילו בחד הוי נזיר; דהא כבר כתיב "מכל אשר יעשה מגפן" — למה לי למיכתב "מיין ושכר"? אלא לאשמועי' דאפי' לא נדר כי אם בחד מהני — דחייל נזירות עליו, ואפילו כשבא לפרש, דהכא חרצן וזג לא כתיבי:
Tosafot on Nazir 3b:11:2.english: "He shall abstain from wine and strong drink" - [This] implies that even with [only] one [prohibition], he is a nazirite, for it is already written: "from all that is made of the grapevine" [Numbers 6:4] — why do I need [Scripture] to write "from wine and strong drink"? Rather, [it is] to teach us that even if he vowed concerning only one of these, naziriteship takes effect upon him; and [this applies] even when he comes to specify [individual prohibitions], for here [in this verse], grape seed and grape skin are not written.

Tosafot on Nazir 3b:12:1.english: "To prohibit wine of a mitzvah like optional wine" - That is to say, [this is derived from] the superfluous verse of "He shall abstain from wine and strong drink" (Numbers 6:3).

Tosafot on Nazir 3b:13:1.hebrew: מאי היא קידושא ואבדלתא מושבע ועומד מהר סיני הוא - דקדוש היום דאורייתא, ואיך תחול עליו נזירות? וקשה, דאדרבה, להכי איצטריך קרא מיותר — לומר דחייל עליה נזירות! ועוד קשה: מאי משני בתר הכי: כגון שנשבע לשתות וחזר ונדר בנזיר, דאתיא נזירות וחייל אשבועה? מ"מ תקשי לו: הרי מושבע ועומד מהר סיני! כלומר, דאין מושבע ועומד גדול מזה שנשבע לשתות. ועוד קשה: דקדוש היום לאו דאורייתא הוא; דנהי נמי דכתיב "זכור", ודרשינן "זוכרהו על היין" — אסמכתא הוא. לכ"נ לר"ת, דגרסינן בתמיה: "וכי מושבע ועומד מהר סיני?!" — כלומר: ל"ל קרא מיותר לאסור יין מצוה? וכי מושבע וכו'? דנהי דקידוש היום דאורייתא, על היין לאו דאורייתא — ד"זוכרהו על היין" אסמכתא. והשתא משני: כגון שנשבע לשתות, וקמ"ל קרא יתירא דחייל עליה, אע"ג שנשבע לשתות:
Tosafot on Nazir 3b:13:1.english: "What is it? Kiddush and Havdalah? He is [already] sworn and obligated from Mount Sinai" - [The Gemara initially understands this to mean] that the sanctification of the day is from the Torah, and how could naziriteship take effect upon him [to override that obligation]? Yet this is difficult: on the contrary, that is [precisely] why a superfluous verse was necessary — to state that naziriteship takes effect upon him! And furthermore, it is difficult: what is [the resolution] that [the Gemara] answers afterward: "[It is necessary for a case] such as where he swore to drink and then vowed as a nazirite, that the naziriteship comes and takes effect upon the oath"? In any case, let the question be asked against him: "Behold, he is sworn and obligated from Mount Sinai!" That is to say, there is no one "sworn and obligated" greater than this person who swore to drink! And furthermore, it is difficult: [reciting] the sanctification of the day [over wine] is not from the Torah! For even though it is written: "Remember [the Sabbath day]" (Exodus 20:8), and we expound: "Remember it over wine," that is merely an asmakhta. Therefore, it appears to Rabbeinu Tam that we read [the Gemara's statement] with astonishment: "And is he sworn and obligated from Mount Sinai?!" That is to say: Why do I need a superfluous verse to prohibit wine of a mitzva? Is he sworn [and obligated from Mount Sinai to drink wine], etc.? For although the sanctification of the day is from the Torah, [reciting it] over wine is not from the Torah, since "Remember it over wine" is merely an asmakhta. And now [the Gemara] answers: [The verse is necessary for a case] such as where he swore to drink, and the superfluous verse teaches us that [the naziriteship] takes effect upon him even though he had sworn to drink.

Tosafot on Nazir 3b:2:1.hebrew: צפורי נזיר טמא קיבל עליה - פירוש: מצות נזירות, דשייכא בהו צפורי נזיר טמא אם יטמא:
Tosafot on Nazir 3b:2:1.english: "He accepted upon himself the birds of an impure nazirite" - Explanation: [He accepted upon himself] the mitzvah of naziriteship, to which the birds of an impure nazirite pertain if he becomes impure.

Tosafot on Nazir 3b:3:1.hebrew: מכדי חיישינן קאמר ולא צפורי נזיר ודאי קאמר אלא חששא ודלמא צפורי נדבה דקביל עליה להביא עולת העוף לנדבה ולא לנזירות - דכל כמה דאיכא לפרושי דיבוריה דלאו נזירות קיבל עליה אלא נדר אחר — שפיר טפי, דלא ניחא ליה לאיניש לקבולי עליה צפורי דנזירות, דחמיר עליה וטריחא ליה:
Tosafot on Nazir 3b:3:1.english: Now, since [Rabbi Yoḥanan] says: "We are concerned" — and he did not say that [the speaker meant] the birds of a nazirite with certainty, but rather [merely as] an apprehension — then perhaps [the speaker] accepted upon himself a voluntary gift offering of birds, to bring a bird burnt offering as a voluntary gift, and not for naziriteship? - For as long as it is possible to interpret his words [as meaning] that it was not naziriteship that he accepted upon himself, but rather another vow, it is much better — since a person does not wish to accept upon himself the birds of naziriteship, as it is stringent upon him and burdensome for him.

Tosafot on Nazir 3b:3:2.english: "He should have [said]: 'It is hereby incumbent upon me [to bring] a nest'" - For it is the way of those who pledge a voluntary bird burnt-offering to say [it] using the term 'a nest.'

Tosafot on Nazir 3b:4:1.hebrew: צפורי מצורע קאמר - כלומר: להתחייב בקרבן מצורע, ולהביא תחתיו צפורים, ולהצריכו לו לטהרתו. ואפילו אין מצורע עובר לפניו — דאי אפשר דליכא חד מצורע דטעון צפורים, ולא נזירות; וגם דצפורי שייכי שפיר גבי מצורע:
Tosafot on Nazir 3b:4:1.english: "He was saying: The birds of a metzora" - That is to say, [he intended] to obligate himself in the offering of a metzora, to bring birds on his behalf, and to provide what is needed for him for his purification. And [this suggestion applies] even if no metzora was passing before him — for it is impossible that there is not [at least] one metzora who requires birds, and not naziriteship; and also, [the term] "birds" is well associated with a metzora.

Tosafot on Nazir 3b:4:2.hebrew: כגון שהיה נזיר עובר לפניו - והיה סבור: אפילו נזיר טמא לפניו, ולהכי פריך: ודלמא צפורין דקאמר — לפטור נזיר טמא העובר לפניו מקרבנותיו? ומשני: כגון שנזיר טהור עובר לפניו, ויודע זה הנודר דטהור הוא, וקאמר "הרי עלי צפורים". ואכתי קשה: נימא דצפורים דקאמר היינו דאם יטמא זה הנזיר העובר לפניו שיביא תחתיו צפורים? וצריך לדחות ולומר: כגון דאמר בלבו להיות שייך למצות נזירות דשייכא ביה ציפורים אם יטמא. ולעיל כי פריך "ודלמא צפורי מצורע קאמר?", לא מצי לשנויי כגון דאמר בלבו, דדיבוריה מישתמע טפי אצפורי מצורע (טפי) מנזירות, משום דנזירות טריחא ליה וחמיר עליה לקבל, ועוד דלשון צפורים כתובין אצל מצורע, כדפרישית, ולא אצל נזיר אלא תורים; ואפי' קאמר בלבו, אין כח במחשבת הלב להכריע דיבוריה לנזירות, דאין זה פיו ולבו שוין. אבל הכא, אע"ג דנזירות חמיר עליה וטריחא ליה, כיון דנזיר שהוא עובר לפניו — אין סברא שיקבל עליו נזירות צפורים טמא, שדבר זה אינו בעולם עדיין, והדבר שקול; לכך מהניא מחשבת הלב לומר דנזירות קביל עליה, וחשיב שפיר פיו ולבו שוין. וכן לעיל כי אמר "אהא", טפי משמע הלשון אנזירות ולומר "כמוהו" לאלתר, אע"ג דטריחא ליה וחמיר עליה, מלומר "אהא תחתיו בקרבנותיו" לאחר זמן כשישלים, והדבר שקול; לכך מחשבת הלב מכרעת הדיבור לנזירות, והרי פיו ולבו שוין. וקשה, דהספר לא הזכיר כאן כלל דקאמר בלבו! לכן נראה למהר"ף, ד"אהיה תחתיו" אין סברא לומר דאם יטמא קאמר שיתחייב בצפורין, הואיל והשתא טהור הוא ודבר זה לא בא לעולם כלל; וא"כ סברא לומר דנזירות קביל עליה, דדבר זה מבורר לפנינו ויש בידו לקבל לאלתר, אע"ג דחמיר וטריחא ליה. ולעיל כי פריך ממצורע — התם נמי הדבר מבורר לפנינו, דודאי יש מצורע בעולם הצריך צפרים:
Tosafot on Nazir 3b:4:2.english: For example, where a nazirite was passing before him - And [the Gemara] assumed [that this applies] even [if] an impure nazirite [was passing] before him, and for this reason it objects: But perhaps the birds that he mentioned were to exempt the impure nazirite passing before him from his offerings? And [the Gemara] answers: [It is a case] where a pure nazirite is passing before him, and this vower knows that he is pure, and [yet] he says, "It is incumbent upon me to bring birds." And still it is difficult: Let us say that the birds he mentioned means that if this nazirite passing before him becomes impure, he will bring birds in his place? And one must dismiss [this difficulty] and say: [It is a case] where he said in his heart to associate himself with the mitzvah of naziriteship, to which birds are relevant if he becomes impure. And earlier, when [the Gemara] objected, "And perhaps he was saying [meaning] the birds of a leper?", it could not answer [that it was a case] where he said in his heart [that he intended naziriteship], for his spoken words imply the birds of a leper more than naziriteship, because naziriteship is burdensome to him and stringent for him to accept; and furthermore, the term "birds" [tzipporim] is written with regard to a leper, as I explained, and not with regard to a nazirite, where only "turtledoves" [torim] are written; and even if he said in his heart [that he intends naziriteship], the thought of the heart lacks the power to decide his spoken words toward naziriteship, for this is not [a case where] "his mouth and his heart are identical" [piv velibbo shavin]. However, here, even though naziriteship is stringent for him and burdensome to him, since [the one] who is passing before him is a [pure] nazirite, there is no reason [to suppose] that he would accept upon himself the [obligation of the] birds of an impure nazirite, for this matter does not yet exist in the world; and the matter is balanced. Therefore, the thought of the heart is effective to determine that he accepted naziriteship upon himself, and it is well considered [a case where] "his mouth and his heart are identical." And similarly earlier [2b], when he said "I will be," the phrasing implies naziriteship more [strongly], meaning [to be] like him immediately, even though it is burdensome to him and stringent for him, rather than saying "I will be in his place for his offerings" later when he completes [his term]; and the matter is balanced. Therefore, the thought of the heart decides the spoken words toward naziriteship, and behold, his mouth and his heart are identical. And it is difficult [with this explanation], for the text [of the Gemara] did not mention here at all that he said in his heart! Therefore, it appears to Maharaf [Rabbeinu Peretz] that regarding [the suggestion that he meant] "I will be in his place," there is no reason to say that he meant that if [the passing nazirite] becomes impure he will be obligated in birds, since at present he is pure, and this matter has not come into the world at all; and if so, it is reasonable to say that he accepted naziriteship upon himself, for this matter is clear before us and it is within his power to accept immediately, even though it is stringent and burdensome for him. And earlier, when [the Gemara] raised an objection from a leper — there, too, the matter is clear before us, for there is certainly a leper in the world who requires birds.

Tosafot on Nazir 3b:5:1.hebrew: מאי בינייהו - לומר: מאי בינייהו בפי' דמתני', בין לר"ל בין לר' יוחנן, אליבא דר"מ? וא"ת: ולישני דאיכא בינייהו היכא דאמר "צפורים" סתמא קביל עליה — דלר"ל אליבא דר"מ מהא לחוד לא הוי נזיר אם לא הזכיר גם "סמוכין לשיער", כדפירש ר"ל במילתיה: "צפורים סמוכין לשיער קביל עליה"; ולר' יוחנן, דלא הזכיר במילתיה "סמוכין לשיער", כשיקבל עליו צפורים סתמא בלא סמוכין לשיער הוי נזיר? ועוד, היא גופה תיקשי לר"ל: למה ליה סמוכין לשיער? בצפורים סתמא לחוד סגי לר"מ למיהוי נזיר, שהרי מתניתין לר"מ לא הזכיר אלא צפורין לחוד! לכ"נ לפרש, דלר"ל אליבא דר"מ בצפורין סתמא הוי נזיר כשנזיר עובר לפניו דוקא; והא דנקט ר"ל במילתיה "סמוכין לשיער", להשמיענו דכי אמר "צפורים סמוכין לשיער", דבלא נזיר עובר לפניו נמי הוי נזיר בהכי. וא"ת: כיון דלר"ל כשיקבל צפורים סתמא לא הוי נזיר אם לא כשנזיר עובר לפניו אליבא דר"מ, הוי ליה להש"ס להזכיר נזיר עובר לפניו במילתיה דר"ל, כמו במילתיה דרבי יוחנן? וי"ל, דלכך הזכיר טפי במילתיה דר' יוחנן ממילתיה דר"ל, משום דר' יוחנן פסיקא ליה דאף כשאמר "צפורים הסמוכין לשיער עלי" לא הוי אלא כשנזיר עובר לפניו; ולר"ל הוי נזיר כשאמר "צפרים הסמוכין לשיער", אפילו אין נזיר עובר לפניו. והשתא ניחא דפריך "מאי בינייהו", דלכולהו, אף בשלא הזכיר צפורין סמוכין לשיער אלא צפורים סתמא, הוי נזיר כי נזיר עובר לפניו; ואי אין נזיר עובר, בצפורים סתמא לחוד לא היה נזיר לכולהו. והשתא נמי ניחא, דלר"ל בצפורים סתמא לא מיחייב משום דסמוכין לשיער בקרא; דא"כ, ליחייב נמי כי אמר "נשרין" ו"טופרין", דסמיכי טפי לשיער בקרא מצפורים. כך שיטת הר"ף נ"ע:
Tosafot on Nazir 3b:5:1.english: "What is the difference between them?" - [The Gemara means] to say: What is the difference between them in the explanation of the Mishnah, between Reish Lakish and Rabbi Yoḥanan, according to the view of Rabbi Meir? And if you say: Let [the Gemara] answer that the difference between them is where he simply said "birds" without specification when accepting [the vow] upon himself — that according to Reish Lakish, according to Rabbi Meir, from this alone he does not become a nazirite unless he also mentioned "juxtaposed to hair," as Reish Lakish explained in his statement: "He accepted upon himself birds juxtaposed to hair"; whereas according to Rabbi Yoḥanan, who did not mention "juxtaposed to hair" in his statement, when he accepts upon himself "birds" without specification, without [mentioning] "juxtaposed to hair," he becomes a nazirite? And furthermore, that itself should be difficult for Reish Lakish: Why does he require [mention of] "juxtaposed to hair"? With "birds" without specification alone it should be sufficient for Rabbi Meir for him to become a nazirite, for the Mishnah according to Rabbi Meir mentioned only "birds" alone! Therefore, it appears [correct] to explain that according to Reish Lakish, according to Rabbi Meir, with "birds" without specification he becomes a nazirite specifically when a nazirite was passing before him; and that which Reish Lakish stated in his formulation "juxtaposed to hair" was to inform us that when he said "birds juxtaposed to hair," even without a nazirite passing before him he also becomes a nazirite thereby. And if you say: Since according to Reish Lakish, when he accepts "birds" without specification he does not become a nazirite unless a nazirite was passing before him according to Rabbi Meir, the Gemara should have mentioned "a nazirite was passing before him" in the statement of Reish Lakish, just as in the statement of Rabbi Yoḥanan! And it can be answered: That is why [the Gemara] mentioned it more [specifically] in the statement of Rabbi Yoḥanan than in the statement of Reish Lakish, because for Rabbi Yoḥanan it is definitive that even when he said "The birds juxtaposed to hair are upon me," he becomes [a nazirite] only when a nazirite was passing before him; whereas according to Reish Lakish, he becomes a nazirite when he said "birds juxtaposed to hair" even if no nazirite was passing before him. And now it is well that [the Gemara] asks "What is the difference between them?" — for according to both of them, even when he did not mention "birds juxtaposed to hair" but rather "birds" without specification, he becomes a nazirite when a nazirite was passing before him; and if a nazirite was not passing, with "birds" without specification alone he would not be a nazirite according to both of them. And now it is also well why, according to Reish Lakish, with "birds" without specification he is not obligated [as a nazirite] because they are juxtaposed to hair in the verse; for if so, let him also be obligated when he said "eagles" or "claws," which are even closer to hair in the verse than "birds"! Such is the approach of the R”P [Rabbeinu Peretz], may his soul rest in Eden.

Tosafot on Nazir 3b:6:1.hebrew: הגה"ה: היכא דאמר צפורים סמוכים לשיער קביל עליה - ר"ל: שקיבל עליו דבר הסמוך לצפורים, דהיינו גידול שיער. אבל כי אמר "הרי עלי צפורים" ולא אמר "צפורים סמוכין לשיער" — חייל עליה נזירות, משום דמשתמע שנדר דבר שיכול לבא לידי חיוב צפורים, דהיינו נזיר, כשנזיר עובר לפניו דוקא. ומשום הכי לא מהני "הרי עלי נשרין", דלישנא דנשרין לא משמע שום לשון נזירות. כן נ"ל. הגה"ה. והר"ר שבתאי כתב שיטה זאת: "מאי בינייהו" — כלומר: מאי בינייהו בפירוש דמתני'? דודאי נראה ליה דר"ל לא קאמר אליבא דרבי מאיר דבצפורים סתמא מיחייב בנזיר, דאיכא למיפרך כל הני פירכי דפריך לעיל לר' יוחנן. וע"כ יפרש המשנה כמו ר' יוחנן, דגם לא יוכל לפרש המשנה שאמר בפירוש "צפורים הסמוכים לשיער עלי", דהא מתני' סתמא קאמר "צפורים עלי". הילכך ע"כ כרבי יוחנן מפרש, ובנזיר עובר לפניו והוא טהור. וע"כ פריך: "מאי בינייהו בפירוש דמתני'?" ונראה שנתכוון להבין כמו שפירשתי בתחילה:
Tosafot on Nazir 3b:6:1.english: Gloss: Where he said "birds juxtaposed to hair," he accepted [it] upon himself - That is to say, [this means] that he accepted upon himself the thing juxtaposed to birds, which is the growth of hair. However, when he said, "Behold, upon me [to bring] birds," and did not say "birds juxtaposed to hair," naziriteship takes effect upon him because it implies that he vowed [to become] something that can lead to an obligation of birds — namely, a nazirite — [and this applies] specifically when a nazirite was passing before him. And for this reason, [saying] "Behold, upon me [to bring] eagles" is not effective, for the term "eagles" does not imply any expression of naziriteship. So it appears to me. [End of] Gloss. And Harav Rabbi Shabtai wrote this approach regarding [the Gemara's question,] "What is the difference between them?" — that is to say: What is the difference between them in the interpretation of the Mishnah? For it was certainly apparent to him that Reish Lakish did not say, according to Rabbi Meir, that with [the word] "birds" alone one becomes obligated as a nazirite, for all those objections that [the Gemara] raised above against Rabbi Yoḥanan could be raised [against Reish Lakish as well]. And perforce, [Reish Lakish] must interpret the Mishnah like Rabbi Yoḥanan, for he also could not interpret the Mishnah [as a case where] he explicitly said, "The birds juxtaposed to hair are upon me," since the Mishnah plainly states, "Birds are upon me." Therefore, perforce, [Reish Lakish] interprets [the Mishnah] like Rabbi Yoḥanan, and [specifically in a case where] a nazirite was passing before him and he was pure. And perforce, [the Gemara] asks: "What is the difference between them in the interpretation of the Mishnah?" And it appears that he [Rabbi Shabtai] intended to understand [the matter] just as I explained initially.

Tosafot on Nazir 3b:7:1.hebrew: האומר ימין הרי זו שבועה - ימין שלא אוכל ככר זה, וה"ה שמאל, כדלקמן. פירוש התפילין — מדהזכיר ימין תחילה:
Tosafot on Nazir 3b:7:1.english: "One who says: 'Right,' that is an oath" - [That is, one who says:] "[By the] right, that I will not eat this loaf"; and the same applies to "Left," as [explained] below. The explanation regarding the tefillin [being on the left arm is] because [the verse] mentioned "right" first.

Tosafot on Nazir 3b:9:1.hebrew: מן החרצנים ומן הזגים - או או קתני, כדמוכח בגמרא:
Tosafot on Nazir 3b:9:1.english: "From grape seeds and from grape skins" - [The Mishnah] teaches [this as] "either... or...", as is proven in the Gemara.

Tosafot on Nazir 3b:9:2.hebrew: וכל דקדוקי נזירות עליו - משום דנזיר שמשון מותר ליטמא למתים, קאמר הכא: "וכל דקדוקי נזירות עליו":
Tosafot on Nazir 3b:9:2.english: "And all details of naziriteship are upon him" - Because a Samsonite nazirite is permitted to become impure from a corpse, [the Mishnah] states here: "And all details of naziriteship are upon him."
